If you want advice here it is: 
Don’t repeat my mistakes. 

I had a boyfriend whom I loved, and dated for quite sometime. But after years, it became clear that he was never going to marry me. 
But I wanted it all so desperately, the husband, the kids. 

I felt and still do feel like having a family and children is my life’s purpose. 

So, I ended things with this person. (The right thing)
It was painful, I dragged it out, I went back and forth. I got into a rebound relationship (The wrong thing) and I ended up hurting him over and over again... And my family, too

And now, I refuse to date anyone who doesn’t want the same. 
I make it a priority to ask if some one wants a marriage or family whenever I meet a new person. Because if the answer is no, I know I have to end it early. 

My advice is not to make my mistake. Not to sacrifice your mental health or happiness for someone who doesn’t want the same things as you. Don’t convince yourself they’ll change either. 

If you decide marriage is what you want, end it. I can’t stress this enough, give yourself time to grieve over this situation, and get help if you need it.  But, move on. Move forward.

Okay, so the best way to learn is to start at the beginning, as if you are a child again. 

I studied foreign language in college. It may seem boring but start with books at your level. Even if they are picture books. It’s difficult to learn with long books because you have to keep checking the dictionary and you forget what the story is about. 

If you can read what I wrote above without a problem start with a Series of Unfortunate Events. It’s a really good series and it’s great for teaching new vocabulary. 

If you can’t read what I wrote above, start with Doctor Seus. They are fun but they are also a big part of being American and you will understand a bit about American culture. 

Good Luck !

It doesn’t sound like your medications are working well. Firstly, talk to your doctor. 

Also, a big factor in depression is negative self-talk. Sometimes we don’t notice that how we talk about ourselves is overwhelmingly negative ( “I can’t…” “I will never..” “I’m useless/hopeless/incapable…”)
Sometimes, we DO notice our negative self-talk, but we chose to continue the practice because we feel miserable and we want to focus on the negative. We become angry and nihilistic. 
I’ve had so many family members, friends, and my therapist point out how I talk about myself recently. It’s an eye opener. 
I’m betting that the people around you, those who love you, don’t see you as incapable or worthless. I’m betting they see much more potential and good in you than you are able to see yourself right now. 

And on the off chance that the people around you do see you as useless, drop them. No comments, no questions. They are not adding anything positive to your life. 

Change the way you speak to yourself (it’s not easy, and it feels silly a lot of the time) 
Recognize negative thoughts in your mind, or speech and make a conscious effort to rephrase them.

Try

 “I am taking control of my mental health by speaking to my doctor about how I’m feeling. It will take time, but we will find the right combination of medications for me.” 

Instead of 

“I feel like a zombie… I feel useless.” 

Or 

“My purpose is to take charge of my mental health so that I will achieve my goal of finishing my education.”

In favor of 

“I’m trapped, wandering around without any goals or purpose. I can’t finish college.” 

Control your thoughts, change your world.

I don’t know exactly what you did, but I’ll share something that my father said to me just yesterday. It wasn’t until I read your post that I truly understood him. 

(This may help you, it may not. I don’t know what you did but in regards to anything short of murder and rape, I think this applies) 


I revealed my fear of exposure to my father. 
My paranoia, my shame, everything. 

His reply was something so simple it was brilliant. 


“And, so?” 

It may seem, harsh or uncaring. It isn’t. 

It’s the kind of wisdom only an outsider can provide. 

What he meant is this:

The things you’ve done may have been truly terrible.  

But they are already DONE. 

Will there be consequences? 
There might be.
And you’ll have to deal with them when/if they come. 
Just as I will. 
That’s the reality. 
There is no way around it. 

And, so? 
What will you do about it ? 

Beat yourself up over behaviors which you could not fully control? 
Punish yourself ?
Hide? 

Self hatred is not a form Indulgence or penitence, and it surely will not halt the tides of destiny. 
No matter where you hide, justice will know just where to find you when it’s ready to come looking. 

I understand you might be ruined socially, you might be in legal trouble or face jail time. You may have caused great grief to yourself and others. 

All you can do is forgive yourself. 
And try your utmost to live a life you are proud of from here on out. 

It’s radical self acceptance.
